note: migrate_skip_on_404 provides one migrate process plugin, skip_on_404 (class SkipOn404), plus hook_migration_plugins_alter() that auto-adds it to core D7 file migrations (d7_file, d7_file_private, upgrade_d7_file, upgrade_d7_file_private). No config, routes, permissions, schema or Drush. method:row throws MigrateSkipRowException; method:process calls stopPipeline(). Existence check: external URLs via http_client HEAD, local via file_exists(). Medium/hard cases are grounded in a real migrate_plus.migration config entity that references skip_on_404 in its process pipeline: introspection reads which guard plugin a migration uses; execution builds a migration whose file process uses skip_on_404, verified by reading the migration config.

evals.prompt: In a Drupal migration, which process plugin does the migrate_skip_on_404 module provide to skip a file when it is missing rather than fail the migration, and what does method: row versus method: process do?
evals.expected_output: The plugin is skip_on_404. method: row throws a MigrateSkipRowException so the whole record is skipped (and a message is logged); method: process calls stopPipeline() so only the current property's pipeline stops while the rest of the row is kept.

evals.prompt: After I enable migrate_skip_on_404, which core Drupal-7 file migrations does it automatically modify so missing files are skipped, and do I need to configure anything?
evals.expected_output: Via hook_migration_plugins_alter() it auto-injects skip_on_404 into the source_full_path chain of d7_file, d7_file_private, upgrade_d7_file and upgrade_d7_file_private. No configuration is needed - enabling the module is enough.

evals.prompt: How does the migrate_skip_on_404 skip_on_404 plugin decide whether a source file exists for an external URL versus a local path?
evals.expected_output: For external URLs it issues a Guzzle HEAD request via the http_client service and treats a RequestException as missing; for local paths it uses PHP file_exists().

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a migration named msk_known. Inspect its live configuration and state which migrate_skip_on_404 process plugin it applies to its file property to guard against missing files.
evals.expected_output: The migration migrate_plus.migration.msk_known applies the skip_on_404 plugin (method: row, source: fileurl) on its uri process property.

evals.prompt: On this site the migration msk_known uses migrate_skip_on_404 to guard a file field. Inspect its configuration and state the method the skip_on_404 step is configured with (row or process).
evals.expected_output: The skip_on_404 step in migrate_plus.migration.msk_known is configured with method: row, so a missing file skips the entire record.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a migrate_plus migration config entity with id msk_task whose file/URI process pipeline uses the migrate_skip_on_404 skip_on_404 plugin (method: row) so that a missing source file skips the row instead of failing. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create config migrate_plus.migration.msk_task with a process step that has plugin: skip_on_404 (e.g. on a uri property, method: row, source: fileurl). Verified by reading the migration config for a skip_on_404 process plugin.

evals.prompt: Some of the files I'm importing don't exist any more and they crash my import. Set up a migration called msk_task that just quietly skips a row when its file is missing, using the migrate_skip_on_404 module. Make it live on this site.
evals.expected_output: Same verified end state as migrate_skip_on_404-build-migration: config migrate_plus.migration.msk_task exists with a skip_on_404 process plugin in its pipeline.
